subject: KPI signal handoff + QBR prep — owners & action plan
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Mark Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: June dashboard: signal handoff for leadership + QBR prep

Folks — sending the June snapshot and a compact ask list. I pulled the heatmap and flagged three signals that should be in the QBR narrative:

- Latency:  p95 across hosted API increased 8% week-over-week (spike on 6/1 tied to a rollout).
- Cost-per-1M tokens: up 12% month-over-month; observed higher cold-starts on smaller model variants.
- Uptime: 99.92% last 30d (one zone-level incident on 5/29, mitigations applied).
- Usage: new enterprise customers contributed a ~20% increase in sustained throughput overnight (region: us-west).

Attached is a 2-page heatmap and a QBR prep checklist. Can each of you take the owners' row below and confirm commitments by EOD 6/7? I want a short blurb we can paste into the QBR slide deck.

Proposed owners:
- Markus: latency investigation + rollback window details
- Irene: uptime incident timeline and mitigations
- Laura: cost narrative (drivers + short-term levers)

Key ask: 2–3 bullet summary per owner, plus a short action list (who does what, by when).

Thanks —
Avery
Avery Johnson
Director, Platform Operations

Thanks Avery — quick update from infra side. Initial read: the p95 spike correlates with a model variant rollout where batch size tuning was not applied consistently across zones. Action plan: 

1) Immediate: revert the variant in us-west (rollout window 6/9 02:00–03:00 UTC) — ON CALL: infra-sre.
2) Short-term (next 48h): enforce kernel/quantization parity in the deployment pipeline and add preflight perf check.
3) QBR note (2 bullets): cause + mitigation + rollback ETA.

I'll draft the two bullets and drop into the shared drive by EOD 6/7 (uploading to the QBR folder).

Markus

Thanks — timeline and owners are clear. Uptime incident summary for QBR:

- Incident window: 2027-05-29 03:18–03:47 UTC (zone failover during a dependent storage maintenance).
- Impact: 0.08% downtime for hosted API; full mitigation performed within 30 minutes.
- Root cause: lack of staggered maintenance scheduling in partner storage; no auto-fallback configured for that particular storage class.
- Action items:
  * Short-term (48h): add blacklist to maintenance calendar + manual verification for partner storage events. Owner: Irene.
  * Mid-term (2 weeks): implement automatic fallback to secondary storage class for critical KV; owner: infra eng (Markus assigned).

I'll attach a short incident timeline and the message we sent to affected customers for transparency.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: June dashboard: signal handoff for leadership + QBR prep

Attaching a very short cost narrative and recommended levers. Summary for the slide: 

- Driver: increased usage from two new enterprise tenants + higher cold-start rate on smaller variants due to bursty traffic patterns.
- Immediate levers (to keep in QBR talking points):
  1) Adjust autoscale thresholds for smaller variants (ops/config change) — owner: Laa (Irene to coordinate).
  2) Apply opportunistic batching policy for bursty endpoints (prod experiments next week) — owner: infra experiments (Markus).
  3) Temporary reserve on heavier quantized variants during known business windows (sales ops/finance to approve) — owner: Laura to coordinate with Finance.

I'll prepare the 2-line summary and a single-slide note for the QBR deck by Friday 6/11.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Great — thanks all for the quick turn. Final checklist before I lock the deck: 

- Markus: confirm rollback window executed and provide a single metric (p95 before/after) by EOD 6/11.
- Irene: upload incident timeline + customer message to the QBR folder (marked as public slide note) by noon PT 6/11.
- Laura: cost summary + Finance alignment note (who signs off on temporary reserves) by 5pm PT 6/11.

Other items: Claire from Acme AI requested a short follow-up to review their usage pattern (they're in the new-tenant cohort). Should we offer a 30-minute walkthrough next week? I propose Monday 6/14 10:00 PT; CC'ing Claire in a separate thread.

If all items are green I'll consolidate into a single QBR slide and circulate to execs Saturday morning.

Thanks —
Avery
